page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a compute-focused instance powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, supported by 504 MB of shared L3 cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Memory allocation totals 576 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-optimized 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. This instance type contains no integrated GPUs, bundled local storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage and external networking components.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing power, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 312098.53 and a PassMark CPU rating of 177439.07. Instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix accelerators, enable strong performance across PassMark extended instructions and encryption workloads. Memory subsystems deliver high sustained throughput, achieving 1088.77 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 448.45 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks. Benchmark metrics also highlight exceptional concurrency capabilities, reaching 400.41 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 199.23 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and superior throughput in Clang software compilation and ray tracing.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the high vCPU density maximizes compute throughput per instance footprint. However, the 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio makes it less appropriate for memory-intensive in-memory databases requiring large footprints per core, while the lack of local NVMe disks necessitates dependence on external network block storage for input/output operations. Consequently, the c4-highcpu-288 is best suited for parallel computing, large-scale software compilation pipelines, CPU-based machine learning inference utilizing AMX extensions, and horizontally scaled static web and caching services.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-288 is a high-density compute-focused instance utilizing Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. It features 144 physical cores, 288 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 2.3 GHz, 504 MB of L3 cache, and 576 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The configuration excludes local disk storage and discrete GPUs, routing persistent storage through network block volumes. Top-tier benchmark results in multi-core stress testing, Clang software builds, and ray tracing confirm strong parallel execution capabilities, reinforced by advanced vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX. Memory throughput exceeds 1 TB/sec on uncached reads, while static web throughput reaches 199.23 GB/sec and Redis operations surpass 400 million per second. This instance delivers high resource efficiency for compute-bound tasks, making it suited for large-scale software compilation, distributed simulation workloads, CPU-driven matrix inference, and high-throughput caching applications.
